commands.author: omarshahine

target.title: fix(imessage): prevent duplicate messages after delayed sends
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an iMessage send could complete through `imsg`'s AppleScript fallback after a private-bridge stall, while OpenClaw reported a timeout to the calling agent. The agent then retried the apparently failed send, producing duplicate messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dedicated send timeout is increased from 150 seconds to 180 seconds. This lets the outer RPC outlive `imsg`'s 150-second bridge deadline plus its fallback verification window, while leaving the 10-second probe timeout unchanged.

This is intentionally a boundary fix rather than a second delivery-verification implementation in OpenClaw. In the observed incident, the delivered rows stored their text in `attributedBody`, so OpenClaw's plain `message.text` recovery path could not reliably identify them. `imsg` already owns that verification.

## User Impact

Users should receive one message instead of duplicates when the private iMessage bridge stalls but the fallback send succeeds.

## Evidence

### Redacted live failure timeline before the fix

One cron session issued three sends of the same text to the same chat:

```text
09:00:33  send request 1 started
09:03:14  OpenClaw reported imsg rpc timeout (send); outgoing row 7080 persisted
09:03:19  calling agent retried
09:05:57  OpenClaw reported imsg rpc timeout (send); outgoing row 7081 persisted
09:06:19  calling agent used direct imsg send; outgoing row 7082 persisted
```

Recipient and message text are omitted. The matching timeout and persistence timestamps show that the first two sends completed at the point the 150-second outer timer rejected them.

### Dependency and caller contract

- `imsg` assigns send actions a [150-second bridge deadline](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/IMsgCore/IMsgBridgeProtocol.swift#L28-L39), which its [bridge client enforces](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/IMsgCore/IMsgBridgeClient.swift#L97-L121).
- Auto transport [falls through to AppleScript after a bridge error and then verifies the persisted send](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/imsg/RPCServer%2BHandlers.swift#L271-L320).
- The persisted-message verifier [polls for up to 8 seconds](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/imsg/SentMessageVerifier.swift#L13-L26).
- OpenClaw selects the dedicated default in [`sendMessageIMessage`](https://github.com/omarshahine/openclaw/blob/fce7399810c/extensions/imessage/src/send.ts#L720-L725) and [passes it to the single RPC request](https://github.com/omarshahine/openclaw/blob/fce7399810c/extensions/imessage/src/send.ts#L871-L885). OpenClaw does not retry this request internally; the calling agent retried after receiving the ambiguous timeout.

### Deterministic delayed-boundary proof

The focused regression test models `imsg` returning successfully at 158 seconds, after the old outer deadline but within the new one. It asserts that the send resolves with the fallback message GUID and that OpenClaw makes exactly one RPC request.

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       52 passed (52)
```

Command: `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts`

### Live patched-build proof

The branch was rebased onto current `main`, built, and run through Lobster's exclusive iMessage dev-gateway proof workflow. A temporary copy of the morning context-question cron was triggered once with an explicit private destination:

```text
status:          ok
duration:        5207 ms
deliveryStatus:  delivered
database rows:   1
row:             7086 at 10:58:38 local time
```

The recipient, message text, and GUID are omitted. The unique output persisted as exactly one outgoing row. This live run completed through the normal fast bridge path; the 158-second fallback boundary is covered deterministically above because forcing a real bridge stall would require restarting Messages with a stale readiness marker and would introduce an avoidable delivery race.

After proof, the temporary dev cron was removed, the dev gateway stopped, and production was restored healthy on port 18789 with exactly one `imsg rpc` process.

Additional validation:

- Full branch build passed on current `main`.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Final Codex branch autoreview: no findings; patch rated correct with 0.94 confidence.

AI-assisted: diagnosis, implementation, test updates, and independent review were performed with Codex under maintainer supervision.
